lessons: Start with a vivid, surprising claim or question that creates immediate curiosity – videos whose hook lines were bold facts or sensory‑rich statements (e.g., “This shark is older than the United States”, “Pluto seemed like our solar system’s edge…”) kept >1.0 of viewers past 10 %

Avoid dense factual exposition in the first 10 % – the biggest audience drops (loss > 0.2) all occurred when the script jumped straight into detailed explanations or background info (e.g., maple‑sap fact, garlic‑chemical detail)

Use sensory or visual language that paints a picture – hooks that described a feeling or scene (“Gulping ice water after a hot pepper…”, “Fresh pineapple is literally eating you back”) correlated with the highest 10 % retention values
Do not repeat the same idea within the opening segment – videos that duplicated a line or re‑stated the same fact suffered a second large drop (e.g., guardrail and windshield duplicate lines)
worst_moment_types: Repeated or redundant explanations in the first half
Straight‑forward exposition without a curiosity hook
best_hook_types: Surprising, bold claim (e.g., “This shark is older than the United States”)
Sensory‑rich description that evokes a vivid image or feeling
Rhetorical question or intriguing “Why …?” phrasing that promises an answer
